newsitem.title: UK: Cellnet subscribers increase to 2.68 million.
newsitem.headline: Cellnet subscribers increase to 2.68 million.

text.p: British mobile phone company Cellnet said on Friday it had a total of 2.68 million UK customers at the end of 1996, up from 2.3 million a year earlier.

The company said it had added 143,000 net new subscribers in the final quarter of 1996, against 215,000 in the last three months of 1995. However, quarterly growth was well ahead of the previous July-September 1996 quarter when Cellnet reported 84,100 net connections.

Cellnet said the final quarter of 1996 had been its best ever for connections to its digital service, with 229,000 new customers. This compares to 159,000 for the previous quarter and brings Cellnet's total number of digital customers to 883,000.
Cellnet is a joint venture between British Telecom, which owns 60 percent, and Securicor Group, which has the remaining 40 percent.
Vodafone Group Plc, Britain's largest mobile 'phone company, said on Thursday it had a total UK subscriber base of 2.8 million at the end of 1996.
